channel.title: Pier & Point · The Canyon
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for The Canyon (Mission Rock), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Added · The Canyon: The record had no address
item.description: The record had no address. The Assessor's active lot 8719B002 lists the address 1011-1023 3rd St. Added as the record's address. Source: https://data.sf.gov/resource/acdm-wktn.json?blklot=8719B002.

item.title: Correction · The Canyon: The earlier row (2026-09-24) "A 24-story, 283-unit residential building's…
item.description: The earlier row (2026-09-24) "A 24-story, 283-unit residential building's site permit was approved" (2020-10-26). DataSF, permit 201910073782: "number_of_proposed_stories":"24","description":"to erect a 24 story, type 1a , 283 residential building","status":"approved","issued_date":null. The record's other sources (MVRDV, SF YIMBY) give 23. Story counts differ between sources; none is picked here. The earlier row is left as written. Source: https://data.sfgov.org/resource/i98e-djp9.json?permit_number=201910073782.

item.title: Correction · The Canyon: The 2026-09-22 row cites Hoodline (Nov 8, 2025) for a 4,133-square-foot…
item.description: The 2026-09-22 row cites Hoodline (Nov 8, 2025) for a 4,133-square-foot unit and "on Tuesday", and an SF Standard article of July 12, 2026 saying it "opened in January". SF Standard, 2026-01-09: "has made the leap from pandemic-era side hustle to 4,100-square-foot restaurant"; "Address 1023 Third St., Mission Bay". No Hoodline article was found or read, and the July 12 article was not re-read, so the 4,133 figure, the Tuesday wording and the January opening are unchecked. The row's own conclusion that the opening date is not settled stands. The earlier row is left as written. Source: https://sfstandard.com/2026/01/09/quik-dog-mission-rock-trick-dog-oracle-park-chase-center/.

item.title: Correction · The Canyon: The 2026-09-22 row gives Sweetgreen's address as 1023 3rd St "from SF…
item.description: The 2026-09-22 row gives Sweetgreen's address as 1023 3rd St "from SF Funcheap's listing". SF Standard, published Sep. 9, 2025: "Popular chain Sweetgreen is bringing its $20 bowls to Mission Bay. Sweetgreen in Mission Rock."; the page read has no street number. The Funcheap listing was not found on search and was not read, so the address has no source read in this row. The earlier row is left as written. Source: https://sfstandard.com/2025/09/09/sweetgreen-opens-another-store-in-sf/.

item.title: Correction · The Canyon: The $59.7 million is the minimum fee subsidy planned for Parcel A in the…
item.description: The $59.7 million is the minimum fee subsidy planned for Parcel A in the Port's 2019 budget memo, based on a 294-unit design; the amount actually received is not stated. The Port reports a temporary certificate of occupancy in May 2023. The Port's disclosure report dates the start of Phase 1 construction to 2020 and the third building to fall 2021 without naming parcels. The parcel's address range is 1011 to 1023 3rd St. SF YIMBY gave 311 bicycle spaces in 2021 and 312 in 2023. Source: https://sfplanning.org/project/mission-rock; https://www.sfport.com/files/2023-10/101023_8b_mission_rock_budget_port_capital_parcel_lease_amendment_final.pdf; https://sfport.com/media/11175/download?inline=.

item.title: Correction · The Canyon: Capgemini's and Sweetgreen's tenant listings now also cite each…
item.description: Capgemini's and Sweetgreen's tenant listings now also cite each business's own live location page, read on October 6, 2026; their earlier sources were more than a year old. Mission Rock Parcel A's affordable-unit count said the 2025 reduction from 102 to 73 units was unresolved. The Port's June 2026 update counts Phase 1's affordable units at the reduced total, so the record now says the reduction appears to have taken effect. Source: https://www.capgemini.com/us-en/about-us/locations/; https://www.sweetgreen.com/locations/mission-rock/; https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/item_11a_mission_rock_phase_2_update_and_port_capital.pdf.

item.title: Correction · The Canyon: The Canyon's record now states: completed in 2023 (temporary certificate…
item.description: The Canyon's record now states: completed in 2023 (temporary certificate of occupancy May 2023) and officially opened in a ceremony on June 21, 2023 (previously given as June 24, 2024); it is the first residential building, not the first Mission Rock building; Capgemini had moved in by April 26, 2024 (no week is given); the March 11, 2025 Port Commission vote on Resolution 25-17 (BMR reduction to 73 units) is now cited to the minutes, with Board of Supervisors action shown as the next step rather than 'pending'; Sweetgreen's Sep 8, 2025 opening is cited to SF Standard and it is the fourth San Francisco store; Quik Dog's opening date is left blank because sources disagree; an earlier construction-cost entry no longer says the cost was revised; permit descriptions no longer say 'ground-floor'; source dates and titles for the Design Controls, the Dec 2021 memo and the Port disclosure report were corrected; and the Jan 30, 2018 approval now cites the Port Commission minutes. Source: SF YIMBY, 2023-06-22 (https://sfyimby.com/2023/06/the-23-story-canyon-opens-in-mission-rock-san-francisco.html); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 8B staff report, 2023-10-06 (https://www.sfport.com/files/2023-10/101023_8b_mission_rock_budget_port_capital_parcel_lease_amendment_final.pdf); SF YIMBY, 2024-04-26 (https://sfyimby.com/2024/04/mision-rock-opens-waterfront-park-starts-leasing-for-verde-san-francisco.html); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission minutes, 2025-03-11 (https://www.sfport.com/media/10376/download?inline); The San Francisco Standard, 2025-09-09 (https://sfstandard.com/2025/09/09/sweetgreen-opens-another-store-in-sf/); Port of San Francisco, Minutes of the Special Port Commission Meeting, 2018-01-30 (https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download).
item.source: SF YIMBY, 2023-06-22 (https://sfyimby.com/2023/06/the-23-story-canyon-opens-in-mission-rock-san-francisco.html); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 8B staff report, 2023-10-06 (https://www.sfport.com/files/2023-10/101023_8b_mission_rock_budget_port_capital_parcel_lease_amendment_final.pdf); SF YIMBY, 2024-04-26 (https://sfyimby.com/2024/04/mision-rock-opens-waterfront-park-starts-leasing-for-verde-san-francisco.html); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission minutes, 2025-03-11 (https://www.sfport.com/media/10376/download?inline); The San Francisco Standard, 2025-09-09 (https://sfstandard.com/2025/09/09/sweetgreen-opens-another-store-in-sf/); Port of San Francisco, Minutes of the Special Port Commission Meeting, 2018-01-30 (https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download)

item.title: Added · The Canyon: Quik Dog, a spinoff of Trick Dog bar, was reported by Hoodline on Nov 8, 2025…
item.description: Quik Dog, a spinoff of Trick Dog bar, was reported by Hoodline on Nov 8, 2025 as going brick-and-mortar 'on Tuesday' in a 4,133-square-foot unit at The Canyon, 1023 Third St, fronting China Basin Park and facing the ballpark. SF Standard listed it at 1023 Third St on Jan 9, 2026 and wrote on July 12, 2026 that it 'opened in January'; the two accounts differ, so the opening date is not settled. Source: https://sfstandard.com/2026/01/09/quik-dog-mission-rock-trick-dog-oracle-park-chase-center/.

item.title: Milestone · The Canyon: Board of Supervisors adopts Resolution No. 193-25 (File No.… (Apr 29, 2025)
item.description: Board of Supervisors adopts Resolution No. 193-25 (File No. 250264), approving the Mission Rock Housing Plan amendment that lowers the minimum percentage of below-market-rate units per Phase from 30% to 20%, by a vote of 11 to 0 (the Land Use and Transportation Committee had recommended it on April 28). This is the Housing Plan amendment on which the Port's March 2025 reduction of Parcel A's units was conditioned; the Parcel A lease amendment is a separate item. (Apr 29, 2025). Source: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, 2025-04-29; Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-07.
item.source: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, 2025-04-29; Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-07

item.title: Milestone · The Canyon: Port Commission (Resolution 25-17) approves cutting Parcel… (Mar 11, 2025)
item.description: Port Commission (Resolution 25-17) approves cutting Parcel A's BMR units from 102 to 73 (26%), eliminating the 150% AMI tier and raising 90% AMI units from 10 to 19, subject to Board of Supervisors approval of a Housing Plan amendment lowering the per-phase BMR minimum from 30% to 20% (Mar 11, 2025). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-07; Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-11.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-07; Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-11
